source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Shakuntala sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.67.1–33 and 1.68.1–9 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): Duhshanta: be my wife; garlands, robes, earrings, gems I bring you today; let all my kingdom be yours (1.67.1–3: the hook); come to me by the gandharva marriage, called the best of marriages (1.67.4); she: my father has gone for fruit; wait a moment, he will give me to you (1.67.5: `wait`); he: the self is the self's own kin and refuge; you may lawfully give yourself (1.67.7: `self`; "lawfully" is carried by the tag on `gandharva`); he sets out the eight forms of marriage and says the gandharva is lawful for a kshatriya (1.67.8–14: `gandharva`; our gloss of it is Kanva's own at 1.67.26: of a willing woman with a willing man, without mantras, in private); she: if this is the path of law and I am my own mistress, hear my condition and promise me truly: the son born of me shall be next after you, the young king (1.67.15–17: `terms`, the turn); he answers "so be it" without deliberating (avicarayan), and adds that he will bring her to his city (1.67.18); he takes her by the hand according to rule and lies with her (1.67.19: `wed`; the union is not shown); he reassures her and goes, saying again and again: I will send a four-limbed army for you and bring you to my dwelling (1.67.20: `army`); he goes wondering what the ascetic will do when he hears (1.67.21–22; not voiced); a moment after he has gone Kanva returns; Shakuntala, ashamed, does not go up to him (1.67.23); Kanva knows it by his divine sight and, pleased, says: this union, made without regard to me, does not break the law (1.67.24–26: `kanva`, `bless`); your son will be great and mighty and will enjoy the whole sea-girt earth (1.67.28: `bless`); she asks a boon for the Pauravas (1.67.33; not used); she bears a son after three full years (1.68.1–2), and at six he binds lions and tigers to the hermitage trees (1.68.5–6): she is then still at the hermitage (1.68.9–10): the cliffhanger. CE AGAINST THE CATALOG PLAN: the plan's cliffhanger was "Years passed. No army came." The CE never says that no army came; it says only that she and the boy were still in the hermitage years later. The line now says that.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Kanva: a great sage, her foster father

loop.prevQuestion: Will she marry a king she has only just met?
loop.openQuestion: What became of Shakuntala and her son in the forest?

strings.recapLine: A young hermit woman told a king how birds had guarded her as a baby.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.text: "Be my wife. My kingdom is yours."
lines.say: Be my wife. [p:200] My kingdom is yours.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (direct speech; no fire): the hermitage yard at coral evening: the king, plainly dressed, a hand held out, palm up; the girl three paces away, half turned from him, a hand on the door post. The card low.

lines.text: King Dushyanta had found Shakuntala alone in a forest hermitage.
lines.say: King Dushyanta [p:60] had found Shakuntala [p:60] alone in a forest hermitage.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): a crane down through the canopy to the small yard, the two of them and the empty hut (plaques: Dushyanta · a king of Puru's line; Shakuntala · the sage Kanva's foster daughter).

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "Wait for my father. He will give me to you."
lines.say: Wait for my father. [p:260] He will give me to you.
lines.note: STORY 1 (answers episode 54's question by 9 s: not yet): she looks down the path toward the river, a hand lifted to it; he follows her look, then shakes his head.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.text: "You are your own to give, if you wish it."
lines.say: You are your own to give, [p:250] if you wish it.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (wedding-turmeric: the low sun through the trees): the king, earnest, a hand on his own chest and then opened toward her; behind him the gold light makes a long shadow of them both, still apart.

lines.text: He meant a gandharva marriage: their own choice, no priest, no witness.
lines.say: He meant a gandharva marriage: [p:260] their own choice, [p:150] no priest, [p:150] no witness.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT (mist-lavender): a slow orbit: evening mist rises between the trees and shuts the yard off from the world: no fire, no priest, no guests; only the two figures and a ring of empty grass seats (tag: gandharva marriage · lawful for a king · Adi 1.67.26).

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "Then promise me: my son shall be king after you."
lines.say: Then promise me: [p:300] my son [p:60] shall be king after you.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · THE CLOSE-UP (meadow-spring): her face fills the frame: shy, eyes down; then the chin lifts and the eyes meet his, level: she sets a price. The word of the turn: PROMISE.

lines.text: He agreed at once, took her hand, and they were married.
lines.say: He agreed at once, [p:200] took her hand, [p:200] and they were married.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (island-gold; answers the hook): frame-within-frame, through an arch of flowering branches: the two stand facing, an arm's length apart, their right hands joined between them at the centre of the frame (the only touch in the episode; no other overlap); petals come down; no fire, no witness. Then the branches close.

lines.text: He left, promising to send an army for her.
lines.say: He left, [p:120] promising to send an army for her.
lines.note: STORY 6 · NEW LIGHT (noon-ochre: the same evening, the sun low; Kanva is back a moment after he leaves, 1.67.23): the king, crowned again, on his chariot at the forest's edge, turned back with a raised hand; she small at the tree line; the army's spears already moving off (tag: he promised it again and again · Adi 1.67.20). A pull back.

lines.text: Her foster father, Kanva, came home and knew it all.
lines.say: Her foster father, [p:60] Kanva, [p:80] came home [p:150] and knew it all.
lines.note: STORY 7 (river-jade): a rack focus from Shakuntala in the foreground, turned away, her head bent (the text: ashamed, she did not go to him), to the old sage at the gate with his basket of fruit, who has stopped and is looking at her (plaque: Kanva · a great sage, her foster father; sub: by his divine sight · Adi 1.67.24).

lines.speaker: kanva
lines.text: "You have done no wrong. Your son will rule the whole earth."
lines.say: You have done no wrong. [p:350] Your son [p:60] will rule the whole earth.
lines.note: STORY 8 (a second real silence before it; release-gold): Kanva's hand raised over her bowed head in blessing; a tilt up from her face, which lifts in relief, to his, grave and kind.

lines.text: Years later she was still there: with a son who tied up lions.
lines.say: Years later [p:100] she was still there: [p:300] with a son [p:60] who tied up lions.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (CE 1.68.5–10; the catalog's "no army came" is not in the text): the same yard, the trees taller: Shakuntala at the door, older; and across the foreground a small boy's hand holding a rope; at the rope's end, a full-grown lion lying down. The source line (top).
